title: cost-optimization-automation-defaults-batching-caching-quant-profiles
author: Priya Rao
description:
Motivation: reduce unit inference cost by providing safe, conservative default automation for batching, prefix/KV caching, and model quantization profiles. This PR implements platform-side defaults and a lightweight autosuggestion engine that recommends per-route batching and quantization profiles based on traffic shape and latency SLOs.

Summary of changes: added a new CostAutomation service that computes default batching windows and cache retention heuristics; introduced quant_profile metadata on model variants and an automated quantization recommendation job; wired defaults into the router so new routes get cost-aware defaults; added telemetry and unit economics dashboards for per-route cost estimates.

Implementation notes: the CostAutomation service runs as a periodic job (configurable cadence) and writes recommendations into the existing route-config store as non-destructive annotations; router will only apply defaults when route has no explicit config and route owners are notified via console flags. Quant profiles are represented as three named profiles (safe, balanced, aggressive) and map to specific bitwidth and kernel hints; the recommendation job performs offline evals on a sampled set of requests (no PII persisted) to estimate quality/regression risk.

Checklist: - [x] CostAutomation service and API - [x] Router integration for defaults - [x] Quant profile metadata and recommendation job - [x] Telemetry (per-token cost estimates, delta comparisons) - [x] Console UI flags + rollout gating - [x] Unit and integration tests

Testing and rollout: unit tests + integration test harness added to perf-canary. Staged rollout: default suggestions are initially only visible in Console (opt-in) and will be auto-applied for internal preview tenants. After a 2-week evaluation window we will flip auto-apply for low-risk routes. Rollback: annotations can be cleared via Console or CLI.

Related work: ENG-3421 (batching defaults), ENG-3478 (quant profiles), ties into the cost dashboard work in ENG-3302.

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the default batching window conservative (10-30ms target) to avoid SLO regressions; heavier batching aggressiveness remains opt-in or gated by traffic size and latency headroom.

docs: add console docs and rollout guide for defaults

review_conversation: Jonas Müller: Left a few nits on the recommendation engine--please add a guard for low-sample routes (done, added a min-sample check).
Priya Rao: responded - added min_sample_count and unit tests to cover the low-sample path.
Samantha Green: Concern about potential regressions for high-SLA routes; recommend default opt-in. Adjusted rollout to opt-in via Console for external tenants.
Miguel Alvarez: Verified perf-canary run shows median token latency increase < 1% for balanced profile, cost reduced ~12% on our sample workloads. Approved.
release_notes: Adds CostAutomation recommendations for batching/caching and model quantization profiles. New conservative defaults reduce per-token cost for typical traffic patterns while protecting latency SLOs. Rollout gated behind Console opt-in for external tenants.
changelog_entry: CostAutomation: default batching/caching and quantization recommendations (safe, balanced, aggressive) + unit economics dashboard; conservative rollout.
perf_impact_summary: Observed cost reduction of 8-15% on internal workloads when applying 'balanced' profile with conservative batching; median latency impact <1% in perf-canary for most routes. Heavy-tail latency must be monitored during broader rollout.
rollback_plan: Annotations are non-destructive and can be cleared via Console/CLI; router will stop applying defaults immediately after annotation removal. Helm chart exposes an operator flag to disable the CostAutomation job.
tests: unit: cost-automation recommendation logic (100% coverage for heuristics)
integration: perf-canary scenario comparing cost/delta across quant profiles
e2e: routing default application + Console flag visibility test
migration_steps: DB: add quant_profile column to model_variant with default 'none' (backfill for existing variants handled in migration script)
Config: enable CostAutomation in staging via helm values and run sampling job for 7 days
Console: enable cost suggestion UI for internal orgs, notify route owners
